issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect StockIngredient to have a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template's StockIngredient class only provides a constructor with an extra boolean parameter (String, int, int, boolean). This prevents students from constructing StockIngredient instances using the 3-argument form shown in the UML and solution and used in the example Main, causing compilation errors and confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a StockIngredient constructor matching the specification (public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity)) in the template. Either add an overloaded 3-argument constructor that delegates to the existing constructor (e.g., calling the 4-arg constructor with a default strictValidation value) or replace the current constructor with the 3-argument version to match the UML, problem statement, and solution.

issues.description: The StockIngredient constructor signature is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement (and the solution implementation) specify a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository's StockIngredient class only provides a 4-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This mismatch prevents students from directly mapping the problem/spec to the template code and will lead to compilation confusion when they (or the provided Main examples) try to instantiate StockIngredient with three arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template StockIngredient API match the problem and solution by providing a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). Either replace the current 4-arg constructor with a 3-arg version that performs the same validation, or add an overloaded 3-arg constructor that delegates to the existing implementation (e.g., public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, false); }). This will align template, problem statement, and solution and avoid compilation/mapping issues for students.
